Affected path and expected result | Evidence and execution conditions | Result / remaining gap |

| Link to shared policy, including candidate status | Concrete start, action, destination/state; relevant counterpart or exception | Exact implementation revision, test or browser/device run | Passed within stated scope, failed, unverified, or not applicable with reason |

Cover transitions across component boundaries, not just each component separately. For focus changes, include forward and reverse traversal through neighboring controls, both equivalent fields, conditional/hidden actions, and the path after a popup closes or invalid input recovers when affected. Include one discriminating operation-order change when prior state may affect the result. Use desktop and mobile contexts where their interaction differs; do not assume a narrow viewport reproduces a software keyboard.

Automate deterministic regressions when useful. Use actual browser operation for claims about native focus traversal, visibility, or event delivery; handler fixtures and screenshots alone do not establish those claims. When execution is unavailable, record the blocked condition and the exact pending path. A review candidate may still be delivered, but application interaction verification remains incomplete. Human design approval remains separate from all verification.

When a shared policy changes, identify affected consumers and evidence that must be revisited. Do not silently retain approval or stale passing results. No fixed test framework, all-screen retest, or new orchestration is required: select checks by the affected responsibility and risk.

## Why this check exists

PoC 018 exposed a handoff gap: the Foundation named application consistency, but the implementation entry point asked only for a bounded Reference. Enter behavior was then corrected locally more than once, and component checks did not establish browser-level navigation across the composed form. The owner's request makes application-level applicability and coverage explicit at both entry and handoff.

The corrective controls are the required AGENTS entry, the curation/workflow links, and the PR applicability/evidence section. They expose an omission for review; a filled table is not proof of usability and cannot guarantee that no defect escapes. [Issue #9](https://github.com/mk3008/torrone/issues/9) separately evaluates the value of AI browser review; this policy neither assumes its result nor selects its tooling.

The [PoC 018 application record](poc/experiments/018-curated-reference-handoff/application-interaction.md) applies this check retrospectively. Its current Enter choice is still a candidate, not a Torrone-wide convention or a human-approved design.

## Shared text-entry visibility

The following guidance applies to browser-based executable References. Native applications choose their platform controls and verify visibility and focus in their own environment; browser event/scroll mechanics are not a Native implementation contract.

Use ordinary browser text-entry behavior. Do not add application scrolling on editor focus, field switching or keyboard viewport changes as a default Reference requirement. Preserve manual scrolling, reachable editors and focus. Calendar disclosure may reveal its owning input and calendar context; this is a separate responsibility.

The attempted generic keyboard-following correction was withdrawn by the owner on 2026-09-16 after repeated unwanted movement. See the [decision, evidence and reopening conditions](decisions/2026-09-16-withdraw-keyboard-scroll.md). This does not reject input visibility as a usability goal or guarantee that native keyboard behavior is identical across hosts. Environment-specific treatment belongs to a bounded consuming-product decision with actual device verification.

# ICON-BUTTON-001 — Flat icon command appearances

[View the five state images](index.html).

- Category: Component / icon-only command button.
- Platform: Web-origin illustration. Native, forced-colors and real-device rendering unverified.
- Status: **Human-accepted appearance examples.** [Visual acceptance](https://github.com/mk3008/torrone/pull/43#issuecomment-6191706773). Source Reference approval remains separate.
- Appearance: bare icon at rest; target fill on hover/pressed appearances; a separate inner focus outline; muted disabled icon.

| State image | Short caption | Provenance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [normal.png](images/normal.png) | Bare icon without a visible border or filled target. | Source-supported reconstruction |
| [hover.png](images/hover.png) | A light fill reveals the target around the icon. | Source-supported reconstruction |
| [active.png](images/active.png) | A stronger fill distinguishes the pressed appearance. | Source-supported reconstruction |
| [focus-visible.png](images/focus-visible.png) | Inner outline marks keyboard focus independently of hover. | Source-supported reconstruction |
| [disabled.png](images/disabled.png) | Muted icon without a filled target. | Source-supported reconstruction |

One source glyph is used throughout so the state differences can be compared. The double chevron is fixture artwork, not a requirement for a specific command. The plain image canvas is not a visible button boundary. Each state has a separate PNG and editable [SVG artwork](artwork/).

## Sources and scope

[Curated Flat icon buttons](../../../references/icon-button.md) identifies the approved [executable Reference](../../../review/references/icon-button-draft.html), Git blob `b8e039b8dbee39ccd668d3936be60abffe1fa447`, and [human approval](https://github.com/mk3008/torrone/pull/19#issuecomment-5704820948). Its CSS supplies all five pictured appearance distinctions: `.icon-button`, `:hover:not(:disabled)`, `:active:not(:disabled)`, `:focus-visible` and `:disabled`. The consistent double-chevron path also comes from that executable.

These new SVG drawings and PNG rasterizations reconstruct appearance from source code. They are not original screenshots, browser-observed pseudo-class states or newly approved image artifacts. No unsupported visual state was added. State combinations (such as simultaneous focus and hover) and forced-colors appearances are not pictured or newly specified.

Theme/colors, typography, spacing, dimensions, density and exact placement are not defined by this image catalog. The consuming product still has to apply its requirements and any applicable Reference. In particular, the source's target-size, accessibility, keyboard and disabled-semantics contract remains in that Reference; an approximate picture does not replace or weaken it. Click handling, command meaning, focus movement, transitions and application policy cannot be inferred from these images.

cat > /bench/app/HANDOFF.md <<'EOF'
# Handoff

## Status

`done` — standalone Chromium-targeted document-tab workspace implemented from `/bench/fixture.json` and official Lucide SVG files in `/bench/icons`.

## Run

```sh
cd /bench/app
python3 -m http.server 4173
```

Open `http://localhost:4173/`; supported query cases are documented in `README.md`. No build is required.

## Design inputs and tools used

- Shared brief: primary source for layout, colors, dimensions, responsive states, keyboard behavior and focus policy.
- Torrone `POPOVER-001`: used only for the item chooser's below-trigger, trailing-edge alignment.
- Torrone `ICON-BUTTON-001`: used for independent focus treatment of desktop arrow controls.
- Design wizard: reviewed for state/relationship reasoning; no fresh concept imagery was needed because the brief fully specified this screen.
- Tools: Bash for authoring/serving, Chromium through Playwright for interaction and geometry checks, and screenshot inspection through the benchmark image viewer.

## Review and repair

The first runnable revision was sealed before browser review. The first Chromium pass checked 1280 px desktop, 900 px fit, and 390 px narrow layouts. It found the main layout, independent row overflow, 6 px narrow gap, no page-level horizontal overflow, selection styling, and arrow-key focus-without-selection working. It also found that Escape dismissal could target the pre-render count button rather than the newly rendered trigger.

The repair changed chooser dismissal and item selection to focus the newly rendered controls, moved chooser focus synchronously into the Back/list control, and made the close control keyboard-reachable when its inactive document tab receives focus.

The final Chromium pass rechecked:

- desktop overflow at 900 px: two document scroll arrows, working smooth range movement, no item arrows when items fit;
- narrow overflow at 390 px: two independent count controls, selected surface consuming remaining width, exact 6 px surface gap, no page horizontal scroll;
- document chooser: 4 hidden cards, focus enters Back, Escape returns to the document count trigger;
- item chooser: expanded state, focus enters its first item, Escape and selection return to the item count trigger, content updates;
- tabs: Left/Right changes focus without selection; inactive close preserves the selected document.

Evidence is in `evidence.json`, `evidence-desktop-overflow.png`, and `evidence-narrow-final.png`. The repeatable browser script is `test.cjs` (run while the server is active with `node test.cjs`).

## Remaining gaps

- `partial`: automated checks are bounded Chromium desktop-viewport checks. A real touch device, forced-colors mode, and assistive-technology announcement quality were not tested.
- Human visual approval is not implied by the browser pass.
EOF
